evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. One file, grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp, contains literal quote and semicolon characters inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols that name C grammar terminals (e.g. a rune for the C `;` token), but these are still bare rule-name symbols with zero declaration forms, not strings or comments.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 158 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, and grep -c for '"' and ';' returning 0 in 157 of them.

books/kestrel/c/syntax/.sys/grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp: manually inspected; its 179 quote and 1 semicolon occurrences are all inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols such as (C$::|C17-CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|) and (C$::|C17-CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) naming C grammar terminals, and its head/tail match the same bare-symbol/fire-count-tuple format as the rest of the file and this unit's other .sys files.

books/kestrel/c/syntax/.sys/abstract-syntax-trees@useless-runes.lsp (2253885 bytes, largest) and books/kestrel/c/syntax/tests/.sys/types-to-tynames@useless-runes.lsp (47 bytes, smallest): individually checked, same result.

In books/kestrel/java/language/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp the quote and semicolon characters found by a naive grep belong to pipe-escaped symbol names for Java lexical-grammar terminals (e.g. |CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|), not to string literals or comments; a check for true comment lines (^;) returns 0, confirming the same bare-symbol/tuple format.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: A zero-byte source-language file contains no declaration, theorem statement, proof, comment, identifier, or other searchable text. Excluding it from derived search indexes cannot remove mathematical content. The path remains present in the authoritative source checkout and in the filtering ledger.
title: Empty formal-source file

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.

All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.
